How many Jews were killed in the Jedwabn.question: How many Jews were killed in the Jedwabne pogrom?
How many Jews were killed in the Jedwabn.answer: Estimates vary widely, from 300 to 1,600 victims, with 400-800 considered most plausible by some historians, though 1,600 was long the widely accepted figure.
How many Jews were killed in the Jedwabn.evidence: Estimates of the number of victims vary from 300 to 1,600, including women, children, and elderly, many of whom were locked in a barn and burned alive.

Who carried out the killings — local Pol.question: Who carried out the killings — local Polish residents or German forces?
Who carried out the killings — local Pol.answer: The direct killings were carried out by at least 40 ethnic Poles (local residents), though their ringleaders coordinated beforehand with German security forces.
Who carried out the killings — local Pol.evidence: At least 40 ethnic Poles carried out the killing; their ringleaders decided on it beforehand with Germany's Gestapo, SS security police or SS intelligence, and they cooperated with German military police.

What was the role of the German authorit.answer: According to historian Jan T. Gross, the Germans were the ultimate authority controlling the fate of the Jews, and the Polish perpetrators coordinated with German Gestapo/SS and military police.
What was the role of the German authorit.value: Germans held ultimate authority/control and coordinated with local perpetrators
What was the role of the German authorit.evidence: According to historian Jan T. Gross, "the undisputed bosses of life and death in Jedwabne were the Germans," who were "the only ones who could decide the fate of the Jews."

What was the role of the German authorit.answer: Sources differ: some historians say Germans (Gestapo/SS) were present, photographed the event, and possibly gave the order to kill, while others argue the presence of German police guaranteed impunity for the attacks, and some (e.g. Strzembosz, Dmitrów) claim the pogrom was clearly initiated by the Germans, tied to Heydrich's orders for 'self-cleansing' actions.

adjudication.question: How many Jews were killed in the Jedwabne pogrom?
adjudication.note: EN cites up to 1,600 (often cited figure) while DE gives at least 340 with a range of 300-400, a large numeric discrepancy; PL is vague ('several hundred') which is compatible with DE but not clearly with EN's higher figure.

adjudication.question: Who carried out the killings — local Polish residents or German forces?
adjudication.note: All three agree local Polish residents carried out the killings, with some form of German involvement/inspiration/coordination noted in each.

adjudication.question: What was the role of the German authorities?
adjudication.note: All acknowledge German involvement but differ in emphasis: EN stresses German ultimate control/coordination, PL frames Germans as inciters per Heydrich's policy, DE presents it as disputed among historians ranging from passive to active roles.
